mainTopic: Laws of kidnapping: who is exempt, the half-slave, the warning against kidnapping, and witnesses to half the crime
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא saying that a kidnapper who sells the victim to his own family is liable. רב ששת changes it to 'exempt,' because an unnamed ספרי follows רבי שמעון, and he requires the victim to be taken out of his family's domain. Next the גמרא explains why the רבנן exempt a father who kidnaps his son. The words ונמצא בידו leave out someone already in the kidnapper's hand, and רבא extends this to teachers and their students. The גמרא then turns to the half-slave. It compares רבי יהודה's view that slaves get no בושת, and explains his ruling through the rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט, while the רבנן read the same פסוק differently. It then finds the warning against kidnapping, and two ברייתות use דבר הלמד מעניינו to show that 'לא תגנב' is about kidnapping and 'לא תגנבו' is about money. The amud ends with חזקיה and רבי יוחנן arguing whether witnesses to only the stealing or only the selling are killed as זוממין. Their dispute depends on whether 'half a matter' counts as testimony, and the case of the בן סורר ומורה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב ששת corrects the ברייתא from 'liable' to 'exempt'
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites that selling a kidnapped person to his relatives makes the kidnapper liable. רב ששת objects based on רבי שמעון's reading of ״מאחיו״ and tells him to change the text to 'exempt.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא recited the ברייתא before רב ששת. רב ששת said to him: I learn that רבי שמעון says the word 'of his brethren' teaches that the kidnapper is not liable unless he takes the victim out of his brothers' domain. And you say he is liable? Change it and say: exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא recites the ברייתא about selling a kidnapped person to his own father or brother, which says the kidnapper is liable. רב ששת challenges this and corrects the wording to 'exempt.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads ״מאחיו״ as a condition: the kidnapper must take the victim away from his family. Selling him to his father or brother never takes him out of the family, so by that reading there should be no liability. רב ששת therefore says the ברייתא's ruling clashes with רבי שמעון and must be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter who memorized and recited משניות and ברייתות in the study hall
'Of his brethren,' a word from the פסוק about kidnapping
Domain, control
'Teach it as...' A call to correct the wording of a teaching
Liable / exempt

phrases.english: A tanna recited before Rav Sheshet.
He said to him:
I teach that Rabbi Shimon says:
"Of his brethren"
teaches there is no liability unless he removes him from the domain of his brethren,
and you say he is liable?!
Teach instead: exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא recited just before this point on the daf
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that selling a kidnapped person to his father or brother makes the kidnapper liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון requires removing the victim from his family's domain, which never happens when he is sold to a relative, so 'liable' clashes with רבי שמעון
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ״מאחיו״ can set a condition for liability, and it sets up the question of who the ברייתא follows.

steps.title: Why not say the ברייתא simply follows the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב ששת's correction. Maybe רבי שמעון holds 'exempt' while the ברייתא follows the רבנן, who hold 'liable.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Maybe that one is רבי שמעון, and this one is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת and asks why he had to change the ברייתא at all. It suggests the two teachings are simply two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two teachings that disagree are not automatically a contradiction. The ברייתא could follow the רבנן, who argue with רבי שמעון. If so, there is no need to change the text.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? A way of saying 'I don't see the problem'
Perhaps, maybe
This one ... that one. Splits two teachings between two opinions

phrases.english: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps that statement is Rabbi Shimon,
and this baraita is the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּילְמָא הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's correction of the text
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's decision to change 'liable' to 'exempt'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different Sages may simply disagree, so assigning the ברייתא to the רבנן removes the contradiction without changing any words

steps.title: An unattributed ספרי follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that idea using רבי יוחנן's rule: an unattributed ספרי follows רבי שמעון. So this ברייתא from the ספרי cannot go against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that. רבי יוחנן said: an unattributed משנה is רבי מאיר, an unattributed תוספתא is רבי נחמיה, an unattributed ספרא is רבי יהודה, an unattributed ספרי is רבי שמעון, and all of them follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת. It quotes רבי יוחנן's rule about who stands behind each type of unnamed teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in question comes from the ספרי. By רבי יוחנן's rule, an unnamed teaching in the ספרי reflects רבי שמעון's view. So it cannot say 'liable' against רבי שמעון, and רב ששת was right to change it to 'exempt.'

keyTerms.meaning: Don't let it enter your mind; that idea is wrong
Unattributed; a teaching stated without a name
A collection of ברייתות arranged alongside the משנה
Halachic מדרשים: ספרא on ויקרא, ספרי on במדבר and דברים
According to the view of

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule: סתם משנה is רבי מאיר, סתם תוספתא is רבי נחמיה, סתם ספרא is רבי יהודה, סתם ספרי is רבי שמעון, and all follow רבי עקיבא. That is why the ספרי ברייתא must read 'exempt.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is used all over the תלמוד to identify who stands behind unnamed teachings.

phrases.english: That should not enter your mind,
as Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
An unattributed mishna is Rabbi Meir;
an unattributed Tosefta is Rabbi Neḥemya;
an unattributed Sifra is Rabbi Yehuda;
an unattributed Sifrei is Rabbi Shimon;
phrases.notes: This is the key line. The ברייתא here comes from the ספרי, so it should match רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: and all of them are according to Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2 and defends רב ששת's correction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the author of the ברייתא through a general rule about unnamed teachings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might follow the רבנן, so it could keep the word 'liable'
steps.terutzMaskana: An unattributed ספרי follows רבי שמעון, so the ברייתא must say 'exempt,' as רב ששת taught
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב ששת's correction stands: selling the kidnapped person to his relatives makes the kidnapper exempt.

steps.title: What is the רבנן's reason for exempting one who kidnaps his son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns back to the משנה's case of one who kidnaps his own son and asks why the רבנן exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who kidnaps his son: what is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic from the משנה, the case of a man who kidnaps his own son. It asks for the source behind the רבנן's ruling and is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה records a dispute about a man who kidnaps his own son, and the רבנן rule he is exempt. The גמרא now wants to know what verse or logic leads them there.

keyTerms.meaning: One who kidnaps his own son
What is the reason?
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: One who abducts his son:
What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ספרי discussion and returns to a new clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reasoning behind the רבנן's ruling that one who kidnaps his own son is exempt

steps.title: אביי derives the exemption from the words 'if he shall be found'
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the question from step 4: the פסוק says כי ימצא, which excludes a person who is already regularly found with the kidnapper, like a son with his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says 'If he shall be found.' That leaves out someone who is already found with him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the reason the רבנן exempt a father who kidnaps his own son. He points to the words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'found' (ימצא) suggests that kidnapping means taking someone who was not already with you. A son is normally around his father all the time, so he counts as 'already found' (מצוי). Taking him therefore does not fit the פסוק's description of kidnapping.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If (a man) shall be found.' The words of the פסוק that אביי reads closely.
To exclude one who is already 'found,' meaning someone already regularly with the kidnapper.
'For the verse says.' Introduces a source from the תורה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
For the verse says: "If [a man] shall be found"
to exclude one who is already found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 about why the רבנן exempt a man who kidnaps his son.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words כי ימצא exclude a person who is already regularly found with the kidnapper (פרט למצוי), as a son is with his father.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges אביי using the verse about adultery
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects that the same words כי ימצא appear in the פסוק about adultery. By אביי's logic, adulterers who are commonly found with certain women would be exempt, which cannot be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: If so, the פסוק 'If a man shall be found lying with a married woman' also says 'if he shall be found.' Should that also exclude someone who is already found? For example, the people of a certain household where men are commonly found with those women. Would they also be exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks אביי's reading by showing that the same words appear in another פסוק. There, reading them the same way would give an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the words כי ימצא alone teach פרט למצוי, then they should teach it wherever they appear. The פסוק about a man with a married woman uses the same words. Following אביי, men who are regularly found with certain women would be exempt from punishment for adultery, and that is clearly wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But now (if that is so).' Introduces a challenge showing where a reasoning would lead.
A married woman.
'The house of so-and-so.' A made-up example household.
Commonly found or frequently present.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But if that is so,
"If a man shall be found lying
with a woman married to a husband,"
would "if he shall be found" here too exclude one who is already found?
For example, those of the house of so-and-so,
where they are commonly found with them,
phrases.notes: He means men who are regularly found with these women, so they would count as 'already found.'

phrases.english: would they also be exempt?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's derivation in step 5 by applying it to a parallel פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading of כי ימצא as פרט למצוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words appear about adultery. Reading them the same way there would exempt adulterers who are commonly with certain women, which is absurd. So the words כי ימצא alone cannot carry this teaching.

steps.title: אביי clarifies that his source is 'found in his hand'
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that he is not learning from כי ימצא alone. He learns from ונמצא בידו, 'and he is found in his hand,' which appears only about kidnapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: I am saying it from the words 'and he is found in his hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his answer by narrowing his source. He learns the exemption from a different phrase that belongs only to kidnapping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in his hand' (בידו) appear in the kidnapping פסוק in שמות and not in the adultery פסוק. They point to someone already in the kidnapper's control. Because the exemption comes from kidnapping-specific wording, רב פפא's comparison to adultery no longer works.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he is found in his hand.' The kidnapping פסוק in שמות.
'I am saying.' The speaker clarifies what he meant.

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not giving up his idea of פרט למצוי. He keeps the same idea and only moves its source to a phrase that appears only about kidnapping.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I [learn it] from "and he is found in his hand"
is what I am saying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא מִוְנִמְצָא בְּיָדוֹ קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the source to a different phrase that applies only to kidnapping.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exemption seemed to come from כי ימצא, which also appears about adultery.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption comes from ונמצא בידו, which is said only about kidnapping, so it does not apply to adultery.

steps.title: רבא applies the rule: teachers are exempt for their students
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that teachers of young children and teachers of משניות to scholars are exempt from kidnapping their students, because the students are already 'in their hand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Therefore, these teachers of young children and those who teach משניות to scholars count as if their students are already found in their hand, and they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws a practical result from אביי's rule. He extends it beyond a father and son to teachers and their students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not only about family. It covers anyone who already has a person regularly in his control. Students are normally under their teacher's supervision, so a teacher who kidnaps a student falls under the exemption of ונמצא בידו.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Therefore.' Introduces a practical result drawn from what was just said.
Teachers of young children.
Those who teach משניות to scholars.
'They are considered like.' Used to compare one case to another.

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן exempt a man who kidnaps someone already 'in his hand,' learning it from ונמצא בידו. That includes a father with his son, and, according to רבא, a teacher with his students.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the exemption depends on the kidnapper's existing control over the person, not on a family tie. This lets רבא extend it to new cases.

phrases.english: Rava said: Therefore,
these teachers of young children
and those who teach [משניות] to scholars
are considered as if [the students] are found in their hand, and they are exempt.
phrases.notes: He means that if such a teacher kidnaps one of his students, he is not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result from the rule established in steps 5 and 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Anyone who already has a person regularly in his control, such as a father with his son or a teacher with his students, is exempt from the death penalty for kidnapping that person, according to the רבנן.

steps.title: A new case and a related teaching of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens the משנה's case of kidnapping a half-slave, half-free person and brings a related משנה where רבי יהודה says slaves receive no payment for humiliation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who kidnapped someone who is half slave, etc. We learned in a משנה elsewhere: רבי יהודה says slaves receive no payment for humiliation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה, the kidnapping of a person who is half slave and half free. To set up the discussion, it quotes another teaching of רבי יהודה about slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה rules that if someone humiliates a slave, he does not pay בושת. Holding this view next to the kidnapping case will raise a question about whether רבי יהודה is consistent.

keyTerms.term: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
keyTerms.meaning: A person who is half slave and half free
We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Payment for humiliating someone
Slaves (here, Canaanite slaves)

phrases.english: One who kidnapped one who is half, etc.
phrases.notes: This is the next line of our משנה: someone who is half slave and half free. רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about it.

phrases.english: We learned there, in another משנה:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Slaves have no payment for humiliation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It moves from teachers and their students to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a person who humiliates a slave pays no בושת.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה say slaves get no payment for humiliation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה learns that slaves receive no בושת. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing his exact source matters, because that same source will later be compared to the kidnapping פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling quoted in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that is the basis for רבי יהודה's ruling that slaves get no בושת.

steps.title: The source: 'a man and his brother'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from the words 'a man and his brother' that only someone with legal brotherhood receives בושת, which leaves out a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'When men fight together, a man and his brother.' This means someone who has brotherhood. A slave, who has no brotherhood, is left out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's source. The פסוק about בושת says 'his brother,' and a slave is not counted as having a 'brother.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In הלכה, a Canaanite slave has no legal family ties, not even to his own relatives. Since the פסוק speaks about someone with a 'brother,' רבי יהודה says a slave is not included in the payment for humiliation.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says
Brotherhood, meaning legal family ties
Is excluded, is left out

phrases.english: The verse says:
"When men struggle together,
a man and his brother."
This means one who has brotherhood,
phrases.notes: He means someone who is legally connected to a family.

phrases.english: which excludes a slave, who has no brotherhood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: כִּי יִנָּצוּ אֲנָשִׁים יַחְדָּו אִישׁ וְאָחִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'אחיו' (his brother) limits בושת to people with legal family ties, and a slave has none.

steps.title: The רבנן: a slave is a 'brother' in מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that a slave counts as a 'brother' because he is obligated in מצוות, so he does receive בושת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: he is his brother in מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן read the same word 'brother.' For them, a slave is a brother because he shares in keeping מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the word 'אחיו.' They disagree about what it means. For רבי יהודה it means family ties, which a slave lacks. For the רבנן it means sharing in מצוות, which a slave has, so a slave who is humiliated is paid.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with רבי יהודה
His brother in the obligation of מצוות

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the question: and how do the רבנן deal with this פסוק?

phrases.english: He is his brother with regard to מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side's reading of the same פסוק used in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן read 'brother' as brotherhood in מצוות, which includes a slave.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree on the word in the פסוק. Their argument is only about what 'brother' means: family ties, or sharing in מצוות.

steps.title: How does רבי יהודה read the kidnapping verses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה can hold a kidnapper liable for a half-slave, since he excludes slaves from the word 'brother.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, in kidnapping, how does רבי יהודה explain the פסוקים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to our משנה and raises a problem with רבי יהודה's view on kidnapping. This sets up an answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kidnapping פסוק also says 'from his brothers' (מֵאֶחָיו). Using רבי יהודה's reasoning about בושת, that word should leave out a slave. So how can he hold a kidnapper liable for someone who is half slave?

keyTerms.meaning: And here, in our case
How does he explain the פסוק?

phrases.english: And here,
how does Rabbi Yehuda interpret the verses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יהודה's reading in step 11 to question his ruling on kidnapping in our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in our משנה that a kidnapper is liable for kidnapping a half-slave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'brother' leaves out slaves for בושת, then 'מאחיו' in the kidnapping פסוק should leave out slaves too.
steps.whyThisMatters: It checks whether רבי יהודה reads the word 'brother' the same way in every place, which is the issue the rest of the sugya deals with.

steps.title: Two exclusions in a row include the half-slave
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה excludes slaves from 'מאחיו.' Then 'בני ישראל' and 'מבני ישראל' each exclude a half-slave. That makes two exclusions in a row, and two exclusions in a row come to include, so the half-slave is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: 'From his brothers' leaves out slaves. 'The children of Israel' leaves out a half-slave half-free person. 'From the children of Israel' also leaves out a half-slave half-free person. That is an exclusion after an exclusion, and an exclusion after an exclusion only comes to include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13: how can רבי יהודה make a kidnapper liable for a half-slave? It shows that the extra words in the פסוק end up including the half-slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, 'מאחיו' already takes care of full slaves. So 'בני ישראל' and the extra מ־ in 'מבני ישראל' are both left pointing at the half-slave. By the rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט, two exclusions in a row cancel out and turn into an inclusion. So the kidnapper of a half-slave is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From his brothers': a word in the kidnapping פסוק
To exclude, to leave out

keyTerms.term: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
keyTerms.meaning: A person who is half slave and half free
An exclusion after an exclusion
To include

steps.confusionAlert: This sounds backwards: two words that each exclude end up including. That is exactly the rule. A double exclusion is read as an inclusion.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי יהודה, who denies a slave בושת, still makes the kidnapper of a half-slave liable.

phrases.english: He holds: 'from his brothers' comes to exclude slaves,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהודה. The פסוק is דברים 24:7.

phrases.aramaic: ״בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ – לְמַעוֹטֵי מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין,
phrases.english: 'the children of Israel' comes to exclude one who is half slave and half free,

phrases.aramaic: ״מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ – לְמַעוֹטֵי מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין.
phrases.english: 'from the children of Israel' comes to exclude one who is half slave and half free.
That is an exclusion after an exclusion,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת.
phrases.english: and an exclusion after an exclusion only comes to include.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק so that it includes the half-slave
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because רבי יהודה excludes slaves, he should also exempt the kidnapper of a half-slave.
steps.terutzMaskana: The double exclusion turns into an inclusion, so the kidnapper of a half-slave is liable.

steps.title: How the רבנן read the same words
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not use 'מאחיו' to exclude slaves, since a slave is a 'brother' in מצוות. So 'בני ישראל' excludes a slave, and 'מבני ישראל' excludes a half-slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: they do not hear 'from his brothers' as excluding slaves, since a slave is his brother in מצוות. 'The children of Israel' and 'from the children of Israel': one excludes a slave, and one excludes a half-slave half-free person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן read the פסוק, which leads them to exempt the kidnapper of a half-slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the רבנן treat a slave as a brother (as in step 12), they do not use 'מאחיו' to exclude slaves. That leaves 'בני ישראל' free to exclude the full slave. 'מבני ישראל' then excludes the half-slave. There is no double exclusion on the same person, so the half-slave stays excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not understand it that way
He is his brother with regard to מצוות
One (of the two)

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute comes down to how each side reads 'מאחיו.' רבי יהודה uses it to exclude slaves, which leaves two exclusions for the half-slave, and those cancel out. The רבנן do not, so each phrase excludes something different.

phrases.english: And the רבנן:
they do not read 'from his brothers' as excluding slaves,
since he is his brother in מצוות.
'The children of Israel' and 'from the children of Israel':
one comes to exclude a slave,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לְמַעוֹטֵי מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין.
phrases.english: and one comes to exclude one who is half slave and half free.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, ״מֵאֶחָיו״ לְאַפּוֹקֵי עֲבָדִים לָא מַשְׁמַע לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reading as a contrast to רבי יהודה's reading in step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use 'בני ישראל' to exclude a slave and 'מבני ישראל' to exclude a half-slave.

steps.title: Where is the warning against kidnapping?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the Torah's warning (אזהרה) against kidnapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know the warning against one who kidnaps a person?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. The death penalty for kidnapping is written in the תורה, but where is the תורה's warning not to kidnap?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה normally gives a warning (a לאו) before it punishes. The פסוק we just learned gives the punishment for kidnapping, so the גמרא now looks for the matching warning.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning: the prohibition that must come before a punishment
One who kidnaps a person
From where (do we know)?

phrases.english: From where is the warning for one who kidnaps a person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question that moves from the punishment for kidnapping to its warning
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק gives the prohibition against kidnapping

steps.title: Two sources: 'Do not steal' or 'Do not be sold'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה learns the warning from 'לא תגנב.' רבי יוחנן learns it from 'לא ימכרו ממכרת עבד.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה says: from 'You shall not steal.' רבי יוחנן says: from 'They shall not be sold as a slave is sold.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two Sages each give a different פסוק as the warning against kidnapping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה points to the prohibition of stealing a person. רבי יוחנן points to the prohibition of selling a Jew as a slave. On the surface they seem to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall not steal' (from the עשרת הדברות)
'They shall not be sold as a slave is sold'

phrases.english: רבי יאשיה says: from 'You shall not steal.'

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מִ״לֹּא יִמָּכְרוּ מִמְכֶּרֶת עֶבֶד״.
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן says: from 'They shall not be sold as a slave is sold.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either 'לא תגנב' or 'לא ימכרו ממכרת עבד'

steps.title: They do not really disagree
steps.stepSummary: Each Sage is counting a different part of the act: one counts the warning against stealing the person, and the other counts the warning against selling him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree. One Sage counts the prohibition of stealing, and the other Sage counts the prohibition of selling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two opinions in step 17 fit together and are not really a dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kidnapper is only liable after he both steals the person and sells him. So both prohibitions are involved. רבי יאשיה names the one for the stealing, and רבי יוחנן names the one for the selling.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree
Is counting, is listing
A Torah prohibition

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
one Sage counts the prohibition of stealing,
and the other Sage counts the prohibition of selling.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי, מָר קָא חָשֵׁיב לָאו דִּגְנֵיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the seeming disagreement in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the two opinions fit together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יאשיה and רבי יוחנן disagree about the source.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each one names the prohibition for a different part of the act, stealing or selling.

steps.title: A ברייתא: 'Do not steal' is about kidnapping
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'לא תגנב' in the עשרת הדברות is speaking about kidnapping a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'You shall not steal.' The פסוק is speaking about one who kidnaps people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יאשיה's source by stating that 'לא תגנב' is about kidnapping. This sets up the question and proof that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes a bold claim: the well-known 'Do not steal' is about stealing people, not money. The next two steps test and prove that claim.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
One who kidnaps people

phrases.english: The רבנן taught: 'You shall not steal':
the פסוק is speaking about one who kidnaps people.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״לֹא תִגְנֹב״ – בְּגוֹנֵב נְפָשׁוֹת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יאשיה's source from step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לא תגנב' in the עשרת הדברות refers to kidnapping.

steps.title: Maybe it means stealing money?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why we say 'לא תגנב' is about kidnapping and not about stealing money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it is about one who kidnaps people, or is it only about one who steals money?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own claim. Maybe 'Do not steal' is simply about stealing property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading it as stealing money is the most obvious meaning. So the ברייתא has to prove why it should be read as kidnapping.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only
One who steals money or property

phrases.english: Do you say it is about one who kidnaps people,
or is it only about one who steals money?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּגוֹנֵב נְפָשׁוֹת, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּגוֹנֵב מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the claim of step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why 'לא תגנב' should be read as kidnapping rather than stealing property

steps.title: Learn it from its context
steps.stepSummary: Using the rule דבר הלמד מעניינו, the ברייתא notes that the prohibitions next to 'לא תגנב' carry the death penalty. So this prohibition is also one that carries the death penalty, which means kidnapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say: go out and learn from the thirteen rules by which the תורה is explained: a matter learned from its context. What is the פסוק speaking about? Capital cases. So here too, a capital case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its claim. It looks at the prohibitions next to 'לא תגנב' and shows they are all capital crimes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא תרצח' and 'לא תנאף' sit right next to 'לא תגנב,' and both carry the death penalty. By דבר הלמד מעניינו, 'לא תגנב' must also be a death-penalty crime. Stealing money is not a capital crime, but kidnapping is.

keyTerms.meaning: The thirteen rules for explaining the Torah
A matter learned from its context
In capital cases, crimes that carry the death penalty

steps.whatToRemember: 'לא תגנב' in the עשרת הדברות is about kidnapping, because its neighbors are death-penalty crimes. This is the source of רבי יאשיה's warning against kidnapping.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the word נפשות. In 'גונב נפשות' it means people. In 'בנפשות' at the end it means capital cases, crimes punished by death.

phrases.english: You say: go out and learn

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה מִדּוֹת שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה נִדְרֶשֶׁת בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: from the thirteen rules by which the Torah is explained:
a matter that is learned from its context.
What is the פסוק speaking about? Capital cases.
phrases.notes: The neighbors are 'לא תרצח' and 'לא תנאף,' and both carry the death penalty.

phrases.english: So here too, it is about a capital case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתָּ: צֵא וּלְמַד מִשְּׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה מִדּוֹת שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה נִדְרֶשֶׁת בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By דבר הלמד מעניינו, 'לא תגנב' sits among capital crimes, so it refers to kidnapping.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: 'You shall not steal' in ויקרא is about money
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא teaches that the plural 'לא תגנבו' is speaking about stealing money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'You shall not steal' (plural): this פסוק is talking about someone who steals money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא. This one is about a different פסוק, 'לא תגנבו', and it says that this פסוק is about stealing money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous ברייתא said the 'לא תגנב' in the עשרת הדברות is about kidnapping. Now we learn that a different 'לא תגנבו', in ויקרא, is about property. Between the two פסוקים, the תורה covers both kinds of stealing.

keyTerms.meaning: Another ברייתא teaches
You (plural) shall not steal
One who steals money or property

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different פסוקים here. 'לא תגנב' (singular) is in the עשרת הדברות and is about kidnapping. 'לא תגנבו' (plural) is in ויקרא and is about stealing money.

phrases.english: Another ברייתא teaches: 'You shall not steal'
the verse is speaking about one who steals money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel ברייתא that sets the money-stealing פסוק beside the kidnapping פסוק from steps 19-21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לא תגנבו' in ויקרא 19 refers to stealing property.

steps.title: Maybe this פסוק is also about kidnapping?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know this פסוק is about money and not about kidnapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it is about stealing money? Maybe it is really only about kidnapping people?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question to test its own claim: maybe this 'לא תגנבו' is about kidnapping too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as in step 20, just flipped. There we asked 'why not money?' Here we ask 'why not kidnapping?'

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say…? (opens a test question)
One who kidnaps people

phrases.english: Do you say it is about one who steals money,
or is it only about one who kidnaps people?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּגוֹנֵב מָמוֹן, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the claim made in step 22
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What proves that 'לא תגנבו' in ויקרא is about money rather than kidnapping?

steps.title: Learn from the context: the nearby פסוקים are about money
steps.stepSummary: Using דבר הלמד מעניינו, the ברייתא shows the context is about money, so this פסוק is about money too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can answer: go and learn from one of the thirteen rules the תורה is explained by: something is learned from its context. What is the context talking about? Money. So here too, it is about money.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with the same rule it used before, דבר הלמד מעניינו. The פסוקים around this one are about money matters, so this one is about money too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same tool gives opposite results in the two places because the surroundings are different. In the עשרת הדברות the neighbors are capital crimes, so it means kidnapping. In ויקרא the neighbors are money matters, so it means stealing property.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and learn
The thirteen rules for explaining the תורה
Something is learned from its context
So too here

steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות use דבר הלמד מעניינו. 'לא תגנב' in the עשרת הדברות means kidnapping, and 'לא תגנבו' in ויקרא means stealing money, because each one matches what is written around it.

phrases.english: You can say: go out and learn
from the thirteen rules
by which the תורה is explained:
a matter learned from its context.
What is the verse talking about? Money.
phrases.notes: The nearby פסוק is 'לא תעשק את רעך ולא תגזל' (ויקרא 19:13), which is about money.

phrases.english: So here too, it is about money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The surrounding פסוק is about money, so by דבר הלמד מעניינו this one is about money too.

steps.title: Witnesses to only the stealing or only the selling who become עדים זוממין
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says such witnesses are not killed; רבי יוחנן says they are killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: witnesses to the kidnapping and witnesses to the selling of a person who were proven to be עדים זוממין. חזקיה says: they are not killed. רבי יוחנן says: they are killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new dispute between אמוראים. One pair of witnesses saw only the kidnapping and another pair saw only the selling, and then both pairs were proven to be lying witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally עדים זוממין get the punishment they tried to bring on the accused, which here is death. The problem is that each pair only testified to half of the crime. חזקיה says they are not killed, and רבי יוחנן says they are.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said (introduces a dispute of אמוראים)
Witnesses to the stealing (kidnapping)
Witnesses to the selling
Were proven to be עדים זוממין
They are killed

phrases.english: It was said: witnesses to the stealing
and witnesses to the selling of a person who were proven to be lying witnesses,
חזקיה said: they are not killed.
רבי יוחנן said: they are killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about kidnapping: the witnesses who testify to each part of the crime
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: חזקיה says partial-crime עדים זוממין are not killed; רבי יוחנן says they are killed.
steps.whyThisMatters: Kidnapping needs two acts, stealing and selling. So the question is whether witnesses to just one act count as real witnesses.

steps.title: The root of the dispute: 'half a matter'
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה follows רבי עקיבא (no 'half a matter'); רבי יוחנן follows the רבנן (even 'half a matter' counts).
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה holds like רבי עקיבא, who says 'a matter' means a whole matter and not half a matter. רבי יוחנן holds like the רבנן, who say 'a matter' includes even half a matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where each אמורא's opinion comes from. It ties each one to an older argument between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says testimony establishes 'a matter'. רבי עקיבא reads this as a complete matter, so witnesses to only half a crime are not real witnesses and cannot be punished as זוממין. The רבנן say half counts, so each pair is real testimony and they are killed.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter (from the פסוק about witnesses)
Half a matter: testimony to only part of the crime
The Sages (majority opinion)

phrases.english: חזקיה said it like רבי עקיבא,
who said: 'a matter', and not half a matter.
And רבי יוחנן said it like the רבנן,
who say: 'a matter', and even half a matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute in step 25
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute depends on whether testimony to 'half a matter' counts as testimony.

steps.title: Even חזקיה agrees about the last witnesses of a בן סורר ומורה
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה admits that the final witnesses against a בן סורר ומורה are killed if they become עדים זוממין, because the first witnesses can say something about their own role.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חזקיה agrees that the last witnesses against a בן סורר ומורה who were proven to be עדים זוממין are killed, because the first witnesses can say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a case where even חזקיה agrees the זוממין are killed. The reason begins here: the first witnesses can make a claim about their role, and the sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בן סורר ומורה needs two pairs of witnesses at two different times, so it might look like each pair is 'half a matter'. But the first pair can claim their testimony was only about the earlier stage, the one that led to flogging. That leaves the death sentence resting on the last pair alone, so they count as full witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees
The stubborn and rebellious son
The last (second) pair of witnesses
Since / because

phrases.english: And חזקיה agrees about the last witnesses
of a stubborn and rebellious son who were proven to be lying witnesses,
that they are killed,
since the first witnesses can say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits חזקיה's position from steps 25-26 with a case where he agrees
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to חזקיה, the final witnesses against a בן סורר ומורה who become זוממין are killed.
